key_insight: ROSE reframes NL2SQL evaluation around user intent: it judges a predicted SQL by whether it answers the natural-language question, not by syntactic match to a possibly flawed ground-truth SQL. This produces a more robust, interpretation-aware accuracy signal.
problem_solved: Execution Accuracy (EX) is brittle—sensitive to SQL syntax, blind to multiple valid interpretations, and easily misled by erroneous ground-truth SQL—so ROSE provides a reliable alternative that focuses on intent-level correctness.
method: Center evaluation on question intent: determine whether the predicted SQL fulfills the question’s intent rather than matching ground-truth SQL text.
Compare outcomes at the answer/intent level (e.g., result equivalence, intent alignment) so semantically equivalent but syntactically different SQLs are treated as correct.
Design robustness to ambiguous questions and noisy ground-truth by accommodating multiple valid interpretations and ignoring superficial SQL differences.
impact: ROSE yields more trustworthy model comparisons, uncovers evaluation false negatives caused by ground-truth errors, and guides practitioners toward models that actually satisfy user intent rather than models that mimic dataset annotations.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Question -> Predicted SQL + Ground-truth SQL -> Execute -> Intent-level comparison (ROSE) vs syntactic match (EX)
Before/After example: two different SQL queries that produce the same correct answer, labeled 'EX: wrong' and 'ROSE: correct'
Bar chart: model rankings under EX vs ROSE to show reordering and reduced false negatives
Icon set: question mark (intent), SQL token cluster (syntax variance), warning bug (ground-truth error), check mark (intent-verified)
paper_title: ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL
paper_authors: Wenqi Pei, Shizheng Hou, Boyan Li, Han Chen, Zhichao Shi
